name: Suwannee River Wilderness Trail: day paddles and river camps
area: White Springs to the lower Suwannee; choose a section
coordinateNote: A long river route, not one attraction pin. Select a section and its public launch from the official map before routing.
navigationNote: Choose an official put-in and take-out pair from the linked river guide; the trail office is not a paddling launch.
experience: Paddle a broad tannic river with wooded banks, spring side trips and a network of river camps for longer adventures. The Suwannee is its own river journey, separate from the historic Suwannee Springs springhouse. Choose a day section with a shuttle or build an overnight paddle around the official camps and river-mile map.
duration: Choose a day section or a multi-day paddle; duration depends on river miles, level and shuttle.
cost: The state lists no fee for the wilderness trail; rentals, shuttles and other public/private camps may have charges.
access: Use the official paddling guide and ramp map to select put-in, take-out and outfitter. River camps are reached by water, with no vehicle or overnight parking access. Holton Creek camp remains listed closed after Hurricane Helene; this does not close the entire trail.

conditions.summary: Official trail page checked October 28; Holton Creek camp closure retained. No present river-level measurement or launch/shuttle reservation.

water: The main Suwannee is tannic river water; blue spring basins are separate stops whose clarity depends on river level.
mobility: A real paddling trip with boat transfers and section-dependent launches; select equipment and assistance with the outfitter.
